newsitem.title: USA: First Team sees Q1 above expectations.
newsitem.headline: First Team sees Q1 above expectations.

text.p: First Team Sports Inc, which makes in-line skates, said Tuesday it expects results for the first quarter ended May 31 to exceed analysts' estimates.
The company said it expects revenues to slightly exceed $26 million, while earnings will range from $0.31 to $0.33 a share.
Analysts' expectations are for revenues of $25-$26 million and earnings of $0.28-$0.30 a share.
In the year-ago first quarter it earned $0.48 a share on sales of $30.6 million.

"The in-line category is still feeling the effects of some excess inventory in the marketplace," John Egart, president, said in a statement. "This, coupled with poor spring weather conditions throughout some key retail areas in the U.S. and Europe, has kept sales below the previous year."
However, he said company efforts to build its UltraWheels branded products had resulted in a modest increase over last year's first quarter sales for that product line.

"Although we are still working through what we believe to be the end of an excess inventory situation at retail, especially the lower-priced products, we are realizing good results from our new spring offerings," Egart said.

He said First Team was late in delivering its new UltraWheels Softec line to retailers, which also delayed the re-order business in the first quarter. But he said the line has been very well received by consumers and initial sales are encouraging.
"In addition, we believe we are continuing to gain shelf space with both new and existing customers," Egart said.
